summary: The implementation satisfies all 14 FRs, all 10 NFRs and all 8 ACs, and conforms to every load-bearing constraint in the design. I settled by execution the three things a source read cannot: router-stack introspection confirms the registration order is route -> path-less catch-all -> 4-arity error handler LAST with fn.length===4, so Express genuinely classifies it as error middleware and AC-8 is not silently broken; fault injection proves the 500 path emits JSON with no stack trace and no HTML; and jest exits 0 under a completely empty environment via 'env -i', which is the real test of the design SS6.2 downstream contract. Zero code defects. Both nits are imprecisions in the spec documents rather than the code, no code change is warranted, and refinement_packets is deliberately empty.

findings.finding: HEAD /ping returns 200 with an empty body, not 404. FR-9 says 'A request to /ping with a method other than GET SHALL also respond 404', and design SS4.2 scopes the catch-all to 'every method/path combination other than GET /ping'. HEAD is a method other than GET, so the literal text of both is unmet for that one verb. Express registers a HEAD handler automatically for every app.get() route, so HEAD is dispatched to the /ping handler and never reaches the path-less catch-all. Design SS3.4 lists the accepted Express defaults that review should confirm rather than flag (case-insensitive routing, non-strict routing, x-powered-by, etag) but omits automatic HEAD-for-GET, which is why this surfaces as an apparent gap. It is a wording gap in the spec, not a defect in the code.
findings.evidence: Runtime probe against the exported app: 'HEAD /ping : 200'. Every other non-GET verb correctly falls through to the catch-all: POST /ping 404, OPTIONS /ping 404 with body {"error":"not found"} and no Allow header, HEAD /nope 404. Router-stack introspection shows one registration at index 0 with methods={"get":true}, which Express expands to GET+HEAD internally.
findings.recommendation: Do NOT change app.js. Suppressing auto-HEAD would require an app.all('/ping', ...) or req.method guard, which ADR-002 explicitly forbids ('No app.all('/ping', ...) guard is written'), and answering 404 to HEAD on a path where GET answers 200 contradicts RFC 9110 SS9.3.2, which requires HEAD wherever GET is supported. Remedy is documentation: add automatic HEAD-for-GET to the accepted-defaults list in design SS3.4, and scope FR-9's wording to verbs with request semantics (POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH).

findings.finding: Two sections of the design disagree about the 404 catch-all's arity. The SS3.2 registration table specifies '3 (req, res, next)', while ADR-004's normative code line is 'app.use((req, res) => { res.status(404).json({ error: 'not found' }); });' -- two parameters. app.js follows ADR-004, the more specific and more recently reasoned statement. Behaviourally immaterial, since Express treats any handler with fn.length !== 4 identically as ordinary middleware and 'next' would be unused in that handler. Recording it because SS3.2 is the section a future maintainer will consult when touching middleware order, and a reader reconciling the table against the code could 'correct' the code in the wrong direction.
findings.evidence: app.js:13 is 'app.use((req, res) => {'. Router-stack introspection confirms '#1 name=<anonymous> path=(path-less) methods=ALL fn.length=2'. Contrast design SS3.2 row 2, which reads 'Arity | 3 (req, res, next)'.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile the SS3.2 table row to '2 or 3 -- must NOT be 4', which states the constraint that actually matters. The load-bearing rule here is the negative one: a four-parameter catch-all would be reclassified by Express as error middleware, so every unmatched request would fall through unanswered until the socket timed out, and the 404 contract would vanish silently. The current 2-arity code is correct. No code change.

requirements_coverage.notes: FR-9 is listed satisfied in substance: POST, PUT, DELETE and OPTIONS on /ping all return 404 with the exact body {"error":"not found"}, which is the requirement's intent. The lone HEAD exception is recorded as nit F-1 against the requirement's wording, not the code. VERIFICATION METHOD, ITEM BY ITEM. Middleware order (design SS3.2): introspected the live Express router stack rather than relying on reading -- index 0 = route /ping methods={"get":true} fn.length=2, index 1 = path-less ALL-methods fn.length=2, index 2 = path-less ALL-methods fn.length=4 and confirmed to be the LAST layer. The error handler declares exactly four parameters (err, req, res, next), so Express's fn.length===4 detection fires; a 3-param version would have been a silent AC-8 break and is not present. ADR-004: grep for a quoted asterisk across all authored .js files returned zero hits; the catch-all is a path-less app.use() with no path argument. This mattered rather than being ceremonial -- the installed Express is 5.2.1, so a bare '*' would have thrown TypeError at module load under path-to-regexp v8. FR-11/AC-8, which design SS7.3 deliberately leaves untested and delegates to review: proved by fault injection. I copied app.js verbatim to the scratchpad, injected a throwing route ahead of the catch-all, and confirmed the real error handler returns 500 with content-type application/json; charset=utf-8, body exactly {"error":"internal server error"}, res.text.trim().startsWith('<') false, and no leakage of the injected stack marker or err.message. NFR-9 and the SS6.4 manifest contract: dependencies exactly {express:^5.1.0}, devDependencies exactly {jest:^29.7.0, supertest:^7.1.1}; 'type' field absent and 'jest' key absent, both confirmed by key inspection rather than eyeballing; scripts exactly start and test; main app.js; private true; engines node >=20. Test file (design SS7.2): exactly 3 top-level it() blocks and zero describe/test wrappers; both Content-Type assertions use toMatch(/application\/json/) regex rather than strict equality, which the design warns would fail on the charset suffix; the not-HTML assertion expect(res.text.trim().startsWith('<')).toBe(false) is present at app.test.js:31; block 1 carries all nine specified assertions including the canonical-ISO round trip and the per-request freshness window; the suite never requires ./server and never calls listen(). Re-ran with --detectOpenHandles: 3 passed, no leaked handles, clean exit (NFR-8). Isolation (ADR-001): process.env appears exactly once repo-wide, at server.js:4 for PORT, and console appears exactly once, at server.js:5, so app.js reads zero env vars and makes zero console calls; server.js is the only file touching process.env or listen. ENV FIXTURE CHECK: .env.example and .env.test are correctly ABSENT and are NOT flagged. This project has no config validation schema -- no dotenv, zod, joi, envalid or ConfigModule anywhere -- and the sole variable PORT is optional with a 3000 default, so their absence is the designed and human-approved state per NFR-10, design SS6.2 and ADR-005. I confirmed the absence is consistent rather than merely asserted: no code path reads any env var other than PORT, and I proved the SS6.2 downstream contract empirically by running jest under 'env -i' with a completely empty environment (only PATH to the node binary) -- 3 passed, exit code 0. AC-1/AC-3 and the boot smoke results are taken from the orchestrator's prior verification, not re-run here; AC-2 I re-verified independently. AC-7: README documents npm install, npm test, npm start, the 3000 default with PORT override, an endpoint table, and two worked curl examples whose quoted outputs match the real wire format. SCOPE DISCIPLINE: exactly five authored files, flat, no subdirectories under src other than node_modules, no dotfiles; no extra endpoint, dependency, abstraction, config layer or barrel file was invented; node_modules and package-lock.json are install artifacts and correctly not authored. package.json carries version, description and license:MIT beyond what SS6.4 enumerates; these are ordinary npm manifest metadata, inert under private:true, and are not a file, directory, dependency, abstraction or endpoint, so they were weighed against the scope-discipline rule and deliberately not raised. ACCEPTED DEFAULTS confirmed present as designed and deliberately NOT flagged (design SS3.4): GET /ping/ -> 200, GET /PING -> 200, x-powered-by: Express. Out-of-scope items likewise NOT flagged: absent helmet, CORS, logging, rate limiting, layering and DI are excluded by requirements SS2.4, and their absence is the design working as intended.
